ABOUT KEYCARD

At Keycard, we're building identity and access infrastructure for the agent-native era, where software isn't static but a dynamic, constantly changing system of AI agents working on behalf of people and businesses. Keycard gives every agent a verified identity and issues short-lived, task-scoped credentials at runtime, so agents can only do what they were asked to do, and every action is fully auditable. We're backed by a16z, Boldstart, and Acrew, and our founding team built and scaled Snyk, Auth0, HashiCorp, and Heroku.


THE ROLE

We're hiring a staff-level Software Engineer, Security. This is a software engineering job: you'll write, review, and maintain production code in our token service, policy engine, and gateway. You'd be the first engineer whose whole job is security, working with engineers who already know the field. A full-time security seat matters because security is what we sell: a hole in our token exchange or policy checks hands a customer's agent access nobody granted. You find those holes first and fix them with the team.

Keycard is a control plane for agents: identity, credential exchange, delegation, policy, and audit. It has to hold even when the agent itself is compromised. Agents are part of how we build, and part of how you'll do this job.

You'll also secure Keycard itself: our cloud accounts, the cells we run in customers' accounts, our pipeline, and secrets. You set the controls and lead security response. Platform engineering runs the infrastructure; operations handles audits and customer reviews. When the two jobs compete, product security wins.




WHAT YOU'LL DO


SECURE THE PRODUCT

 - Threat modeling. Trace how an agent gets access, from token exchange through delegation to the per-tool check at our MCP gateway, then attack it: confused deputies, poisoned tool descriptions, prompt injection, issuer and audience mix-ups, token passthrough. Credentials shouldn't leak between hops, and delegated access should end when it expires or is revoked.

 - Assume compromise. Even a compromised agent should be stopped from escalating privileges or crossing tenants. Document what it can still do with its access.

 - Design review. Review designs and code across the token service, Cedar policy engine, MCP gateway, CLI, SDKs, and Console, mostly for who can do what and whether zones stay isolated.

 - Attack with agents. Run scoped agents against an isolated instance and chase the authorization failures they find. Confirmed failures become CI regressions for token exchange, impersonation, or per-tool policy. Example: a harness that follows a delegated credential end to end and checks it never gains scope or lifetime.

 - Customer reviews. Be the technical voice when customers' security teams review or pentest us; operations runs the process.


SECURE KEYCARD

 - Cloud guardrails. Set the rules for our cloud accounts, pipeline, and customer-hosted cells, down to cell isolation and audited break-glass access. Platform engineering builds them.

 - Our own credentials. Keep them short-lived and narrow. Design service identity and PKI, sign what we ship to customers, and manage dependency risk. You also use Keycard to scope what our own agents can reach.

 - Incident response. Investigate vulnerabilities and security events, coordinate fixes, and improve detection. You'll also work out with engineering how on-call works for security.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You've shipped and maintained production code, not only security tooling, and you've found and fixed vulnerabilities in applications or identity systems.

 - You can read unfamiliar code, build an exploit or reproduction, and ship the fix with a regression test.

 - You know OAuth 2.0 and 2.1, OIDC, and token exchange (RFC 8693), and can describe failures you've seen, like refresh-token misuse.

 - You can spot the problem in an IAM policy, a network path, or a cloud audit log, even if you've never run cloud infrastructure.

 - Good judgment about risk. You can explain an attack path, size it, and agree on a fix with the team.

 - Agents at work. You use agents for review, triage, or testing, and know how to check their output and limit their access.


STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE

 - Experience in identity infrastructure, developer tools, or multi-tenant SaaS.

 - Experience with DPoP, Cedar, or SPIFFE/SPIRE.

 - Hands-on AWS security: IAM, SCPs, logging, infrastructure as code.

 - Securing agents or MCP servers, including tool permissions and sandboxing.

 - A security tool you built that engineers adopted and that ended a class of bugs.

 - Public security work: CVEs, bug bounties, write-ups, or OAuth and MCP standards work.


YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

 - Month one: map trust boundaries in token exchange and one priority delegation flow, attack them, and compare findings with our risk register. Review the company security setup with platform engineering.

 - Ship fixes for the findings we agree matter most, each with a CI regression.

 - Build reusable evidence for customer reviews and a triage process for pentest findings; questionnaires stay with operations.

 - By day 90: a product and company security roadmap with owners and incident roles, built from the risk register you now own.


WHO WILL LOVE THIS JOB

 - You'd rather break the product yourself than wait for a customer's red team to.

 - You'd rather fix a class of bugs once than file the same finding twice.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Build at the Frontier: Work every day at the frontier of agent-native systems — shipping, inventing, and iterating on technology that hasn’t been built before. You’ll be given huge autonomy, the opportunity to gain mastery, and the chance to work in a team that holds each other accountable to succeed.

 - Truly Agent-Native Culture: At Keycard, we don’t just enable others to adopt agents — we use them ourselves to build. You’ll help shape an organization that embeds AI into its foundation as an enduring competitive advantage.

 - Compensation With Upside: Market-competitive salaries and generous equity packages (4-year vest, 1-year cliff) give you the security to focus on building — and the asymmetric upside of ownership in a company chasing a category-defining mission.

 - Comprehensive Benefits & Recharge: Health, dental, vision, and paramedical coverage for you and your family, plus 4 weeks vacation, 11 statutory holidays, and 1 volunteer day annually. We encourage at least 2 weeks off each year to fully recharge.

 - Tools That Keep You Ahead: A new MacBook Pro, a $500 stipend for peripherals, and the best AI tools available so you can work at the forefront of agent-native workflows.

 - Remote-First Flexibility: We are a remote-first team prioritizing asynchronous collaboration, with hiring focused in North and South America. Work where you’re strongest — we just want the best.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Inference team brings OpenAI’s most capable research and technology to the world through our products. We empower consumers, enterprises and developers alike to use and access our state-of-the-art AI models, allowing them to do things that they’ve never been able to before. We focus on performant and efficient model inference, as well as accelerating research progression via model inference.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an engineer to lead the optimization of OpenAI’s state-of-the-art frontier models on TPUs. You will own performance across the full forward pass, from model code through kernels to execution on the hardware.

You’ll have broad technical ownership: identifying performance bottlenecks, choosing the most impactful improvements, and carrying them through implementation and validation. We welcome experience gained through either training or inference, with a strong foundation in optimizing real workloads on TPUs.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Optimize model execution on TPUs, improving performance across the complete forward pass and the interactions between model code, kernels, and hardware.

 - Profile workloads, identify bottlenecks, and implement improvements to latency, throughput, and hardware utilization.

 - Develop and optimize kernels, using an understanding of the surrounding model to guide implementation choices.

 - Explore techniques such as quantization to improve inference efficiency while preserving model quality.

 - Build benchmarks and tools to measure performance, validate correctness, and guide optimization work.

 - Partner with researchers and engineers to support new model architectures and bring performance improvements into production.
   


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have practical experience optimizing machine learning workloads on TPUs, through training, inference, or both.

 - Understand modern model architectures and how their computation maps onto accelerator hardware.

 - Can connect detailed kernel behavior to the performance of a complete model and work across these layers of the stack.

 - Bring strong software engineering skills and a systematic approach to profiling, debugging, and validating performance improvements.

 - Take ownership of open-ended technical problems and can identify priorities, make design decisions, and deliver working solutions.

 - Enjoys collaborating with researchers and engineers, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and communicating technical tradeoffs.

 - Have experience with quantization or attention kernels, which would be especially useful in this role.
